---
title: Running R with knitr
---

## Overview

Quarto uses [knitr](https://yihui.org/knitr/) to execute R code. A code block
whose language is `r` in braces, as in ```` ```{r} ````, is an executable cell,
and knitr owns the `r` language by default, so a document with R cells needs
no `engine:` key. Quarto runs each cell when it renders the document and puts
the output in the page.

Here is a simple example:

````{.markdown filename="airquality.qmd"}
---
title: ggplot2 demo
author: Norah Jones
date: 5/22/2021
format:
  html:
    code-fold: true
---

## Air quality

@fig-airquality explores the impact of temperature on ozone level.

```{r}
#| label: fig-airquality
#| fig-cap: "Temperature and ozone level."
#| warning: false

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(airquality, aes(Temp, Ozone)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess")
```
````

The comments at the top of the cell are cell options. Here they give the
figure a label and a caption, which makes it
[cross-referenceable](cross-references.qmd).

A cell can produce a wide variety of output, including plots, tables from
data frames, and plain text such as the printed result of a statistical
summary. The [execution options](#execution-options) control what appears,
and a value can also be computed inside a sentence with an
[inline expression](computations.qmd#inline-expressions).

### Rendering

Render the document from a shell:

```bash
q2 render airquality.qmd
q2 render airquality.qmd --to docx
```

`q2 preview airquality.qmd` renders the document and keeps the page up to date
as you edit.

## Installation

To run R cells you need R and the **rmarkdown** package:

```r
install.packages("rmarkdown")
```

Installing **rmarkdown** also installs **knitr**, so it provides everything
needed to render a document that contains R code. Quarto requires knitr 1.44
or later.

Quarto finds R by looking for `Rscript` on the system `PATH`. To use a
different R, set the `QUARTO_R` environment variable to the directory that
holds the `Rscript` binary, or to the binary itself.

## How Quarto picks knitr

Quarto sends any cell whose language is `r` to knitr. You don't need an
`engine:` or `knitr:` key to select it. A document with both `{r}`
and `{python}` cells runs the Python cells through
[reticulate](https://rstudio.github.io/reticulate/), because knitr takes
Python only when it is already running for the R cells.

::: {.callout-note}
## Migrating from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 chose one engine for the whole document, and it chose knitr whenever
the document had an `{r}` cell. In Quarto 2 each language goes to the engine
that owns it, so `{r}` cells run in knitr whatever else the document contains.
The [engines page](engines.qmd) describes how to change which engine owns a
language, and
[Running R cells on Ark](jupyter-kernels.qmd#r-on-jupyter) shows how to run
`{r}` cells on a Jupyter kernel instead.
:::

## Cell options

Cell options are `#|` comment lines at the top of a cell, written in YAML:

````markdown
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Air Quality"

library(ggplot2)

ggplot(airquality, aes(Temp, Ozone)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "loess", se = FALSE)
```
````

Putting each option on its own line keeps long values such as `fig-cap`,
`fig-subcap` and `fig-alt` readable, and lets editors change an option without
parsing the cell header.

::: {.callout-note}
## Migrating from Quarto 1

Quarto 1 accepted options on the first line of the cell too, as in
```` ```{r, echo = FALSE} ````. Quarto 2 does not. A header like that is
rejected with error [`Q-2-36`](../../errors/markdown/Q-2-36.qmd), and the fix
is to move each option to a `#|` line.
:::

Option values use YAML syntax, not R syntax. To compute a value with R, start
it with `!expr`:

```r
#| echo: !expr Sys.getenv("SHOW_CODE") == "yes"
```

`!expr` is a YAML tag, and it must be followed by a single YAML flow scalar:
see the [YAML specification](https://yaml.org/spec/1.2.2/#73-flow-scalar-styles)
for how double-quoted, single-quoted and unquoted strings work.

::: {.callout-note}
## Migrating from Quarto 1

In Quarto 1, `!expr` also worked in caption options. In Quarto 2 the caption
options `fig-cap` and `tbl-cap` do not evaluate it: a caption written
`#| fig-cap: !expr paste("Air", "Quality")` appears as that text. To compute a
caption, use the cross-reference div syntax with an
[inline expression](computations.qmd#inline-expressions).
:::

### Cell labels

Set a label for a cell with the `label` option:

````markdown
```{r}
#| label: convert
airquality$TempC <- (5 / 9) * (airquality$Temp - 32)
```
````

Unless you want a cross-reference, avoid the reserved
[cross-reference prefixes](cross-references.qmd) (`fig-`, `tbl-` and the
others) for labels.

### Execution options

The `execute` front matter key sets a default for a whole document, and a
`#|` line overrides it for one cell. For example, to hide the code in every
cell and show it in one:

````markdown
---
title: Knitr Document
execute:
  echo: false
---

```{r}
#| echo: true
summary(airquality)
```
````

The options that decide what appears are `eval`, `echo`, `output`, `warning`,
`error` and `include`. Set `output: asis` when R writes markdown that Quarto
should not wrap:

````markdown
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

cat("# Heading 1\n")
cat("## Heading 2\n")
```
````

### Data frames

The `df-print` option sets how data frames print. Set it in the format:

```yaml
---
title: "Document"
format:
  html:
    df-print: paged
---
```

| Option    | Description                                                                                                                      |
|-----------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `default` | Use the default S3 method for the data frame.                                                                                    |
| `kable`   | A Markdown table, made with [`knitr::kable()`](https://bookdown.org/yihui/rmarkdown-cookbook/kable.html).                       |
| `tibble`  | A plain text table, made with the [tibble](https://tibble.tidyverse.org/) package.                                               |
| `paged`   | An HTML table that pages long rows and columns, made with [`rmarkdown::paged_table()`](https://pkgs.rstudio.com/rmarkdown/reference/paged_table.html). |

`paged` is available in HTML formats. In any other format Quarto prints the
data frame with `kable`.

## Knitr options

To set knitr's own chunk options once, for a whole document, put them under
the `knitr` key:

```yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format: html
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: "#>"
    R.options:
      digits: 3
---
```

The `knitr` key also works in a project's `_quarto.yml`, where it sets the
defaults for every document in the project.

The `R.options` chunk option is a convenient way to set R options that apply
only while the chunk runs. knitr sets them with
[`options()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/options.html) before the chunk and
restores them afterward.

## Inline expressions

Knitr cells can compute a value inside a sentence, with either the brace
spelling `` `{r} x` `` or knitr's own `` `r x` ``. The two differ in how they
insert the value, and
[Inline expressions](computations.qmd#inline-expressions) describes both.

## Caching

The knitr cache works per cell rather than per document, so you are
responsible for tracking dependencies between cells (for example, with
`dependson`).

Enable the cache for a document or a project with the `execute` option:

```yaml
---
title: "My Document"
format: html
execute:
  cache: true
---
```

Or enable it for a single cell, and leave the document option unset:

````markdown
```{r}
#| cache: true

summary(cars)
```
````

The other cell options that affect knitr's cache, such as `cache.path`,
`dependson` and `cache.rebuild`, work as they do in knitr. Yihui Xie's article
on [cache invalidation](https://yihui.org/en/2018/06/cache-invalidation/)
explains how knitr decides that a cache is out of date.

::: {.callout-note}
## Migrating from Quarto 1

The command line options `--cache` and `--cache-refresh` are accepted by
`q2 render` but do not change caching in Quarto 2. To force a refresh, delete
the cell's cache directory, or set `cache.rebuild` on the cell.
:::

If you are caching to shorten a slow render, `execute: enabled: false` skips
execution while you work on prose, and `freeze` keeps results from documents
you have not changed.

## Chunks that keep knitr's markdown {#chunks-that-keep-knitrs-markdown}

When Quarto runs a document it can keep what the code produced as an
[execution record](execution-records.qmd), so that `q2 preview` and hub can
redisplay the page without rerunning R. For most cells, the record stores each
output knitr produced separately: source code, printed text, messages and
plots.

For some cells, there are no structured outputs for Quarto to save. In that
case it stores the rendered markdown from knitr as a single block in the
notebook. The rendered page comes out identical, but tools that read the
notebook directly, such as Positron, see one markdown blob instead of
individual outputs, so they won't display those outputs or populate them from
their own cache.

These cells keep knitr's markdown:

- **A cell that includes another document with `child=`.** Quarto reports
  [`Q-18-14`](../../errors/engine/Q-18-14.qmd).
- **A cell in another language run by knitr.** This covers `bash`, `sql`,
  Python through reticulate, and engines you define yourself.
- **Every cell from the point where the document replaces a knitr hook.** A
  call to `knitr::knit_hooks$set()` for `source`, `output`, `message`,
  `warning`, `error` or `plot` changes what knitr writes for a cell, and Quarto
  cannot know what the new hook does. The cell that replaces the hook and every
  cell after it keep knitr's markdown, and Quarto reports
  [`Q-18-13`](../../errors/engine/Q-18-13.qmd). Cell options such as
  `class.output`, `attr.source` and `collapse` can replace a custom hook for
  most purposes, and they don't cause this fallback.
- **Every cell, when the output format isn't yet supported by execution
  records.** Supported formats are HTML, Reveal.js, EPUB, Typst, Word (`docx`),
  PowerPoint (`pptx`) and GitHub Flavored Markdown (`gfm`). Other formats,
  such as PDF, keep knitr's markdown for every cell.
- **A cell that asks for `cache: 1` or `cache: 2`.** Its output appears on the
  rendered page but is not stored in the record. A cell that asks for
  `cache: true` is recorded.
